Some good points, the lack of info in a lot of places is driving me almost as crazy as the interface oddities.

His point about being able to wipe a religion out the turn it's created is really important. I can see why it should be more expensive to buy apostles and missionaries of minority religions but it shouldn't be impossible to, and the holy city should always be able to do it even if the city gets converted hard.

The game seems like it has a steeper learning curve than 4 or 5 and the AI programmers don't seem to have been able to handle that. Even on king difficulty (where the AI cheats a bit) I've had no difficulty winning.

There are are some cool new features like the eurekas/inspirations that can have you scrambling to get certain things done before you have to research a tech/policy to take care of half the research. But unfortunately the tech and policy tree both seem very simplified and empty compared to 5, the two of them together are about as big as the tech tree from civ 4. A few techs unlock almost nothing - some unlock just a wonder (so most players will get nothing at all from it), the entire last two rows of techs add only military units and tech victory pieces and nothing else, so sometimes you feel like you're wasting time by researching a tech.. I see what they were going for with the policy cards but there are a few you'll find yourself using a lot and a lot that you'll find yourself rarely/never using, and it's really annoying when some of them disappear as you tech up.

The lack of diplomatic victory and the fight for control of the world congress makes the late game more boring. It also hurts the policy system since diplomatic policies are basically useless (and there are only like 5-6 of them anyway).

The district thing is interesting, it requires you to plan your city out a lot more before you start improving tiles which makes it more challenging, but the lack of clear explanation raises the learning curve a lot. Also, after the granary and water mill early on, there's no buildings that aren't dependent on a district until very late game when you get sewers. So if you have a city with a lot of water, mountains, or resources you don't want to remove and you don't have room for many districts, your city will be a lot more useless than it would have been in previous games. This is another area where just 3-4 more buildings sprinkled throughout the tech tree that aren't dependent on districts would improve things a lot.

tl;dr in a couple expansions when diplomatic victory is added and the tech tree is filled in properly civ 6 will probably be a good game
